The incident is the second time police have clashed with teachers in the past week, and more conflict is likely as Mexico City prepares to hold the opening game of the Fifa World Cup on 11 June.

Success of far-right presidential candidate, Abelardo de la Espriella, suggests some voters are ‘fed up with politics’

rfi.title: EU tightens migration rules, eyes strategic enlargement in Balkans
rfi.description: The European Union has reached a deal on tougher migration rules that would allow countries to set up so-called “return hubs” outside the bloc, a move hailed by supporters as a practical answer to stalled deportations, but denounced by rights groups as a dangerous step towards offshore detention. Meanwhile, the question of EU enlargement is also on the cards at a Western Balkans summit.

rfi.title: France bans Israeli offensive weapons on Europe's largest arms trade show
rfi.description: France has banned the display of Israeli offensive weapons at the 2026 edition of the Eurosatory international defence and security exhibition which opens on 15 June.

rfi.title: WHO seeks more aid for Congo as ebola outbreak continues to spread
rfi.description: The head of the World Health Organization  met with Félix Tshisekedi on Monday to discuss the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola outbreak, as an aid agency warned the epidemic was likely far larger than official figures suggest. The government said confirmed Ebola cases had risen to 321.

rfi.title: French health minister promises fast track access to mental health for youth
rfi.description: France's Health Minister Stéphanie Rist announced on Tuesday that the government would fast-track access to mental health appointments for young people. She promised that those identified by staff in the national education system as having mental health problems would be seen by a professional within 24 to 48 hours.

rfi.title: Mozambique claims five of its nationals killed killed in South Africa 'xenophobic attacks'
rfi.description: Mozambique has claimed that five of its nationals were killed in xenophobic attacks in South Africa at the weekend, as efforts got under way on Tuesday to repatriate hundreds of others.

rfi.title: New York Times chief slams AI companies for 'theft' of intellectual property
rfi.description: The head of The New York Times newspaper launched a scathing attack on artificial intelligence companies, accusing them of "shameless theft of intellectual property" and of threatening journalism. He was speaking at a global media congress on Monday in the southern French city of Marseille.

rfi.title: Cattelan’s famous taped banana stolen from French museum
rfi.description: A museum in eastern France has filed a police complaint after a banana forming the centrepiece of Maurizio Cattelan’s multimillion-dollar conceptual artwork "Comedian" was stolen from an exhibition.

rfi.title: Africa's finest: Morocco, African champions by ruling
rfi.description: Morocco arrive at the first 48-team World Cup as Africa's highest-ranked side in the Fifa standings. In the second of a nine-part series on African squads at the tournament, RFI profiles a nation making its seventh World Cup appearance.

rfi.title: Gulf states arrested over 1,000 for Iran war social media posts: Amnesty
rfi.description: More than 1,000 people have been arrested across Gulf states for sharing information or opinions related to the Iran-US-Israeli war, in what Amnesty International has described as a “widespread crackdown” on freedom of expression.

rfi.title: Court rejects Rwanda €115mn claim against Britain over migrant deal
rfi.description: An international court on Monday rejected a claim by Rwanda for Britain to pay more than £100 million (€115million) it said London still owed from a scrapped deal to deport migrants.

rfi.title: Guineans denounce an 'electoral farce' after low turnout in legislative polls
rfi.description: Legislative and municipal elections were held in Guinea on Sunday to complete the process of returning constitutional order to the country after the December 2025 presidential election While this double ballot took place without major incident, voter turnout was low.

rfi.title: Ethiopia goes to the polls with the result widely seen as a foregone conclusion
rfi.description: Ethiopia holds parliamentary and regional elections on Monday that analysts expect Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's party to win by a large margin, despite significant unrest across much of the country.

rfi.title: PSG celebrations marred by violence as French authorities report 890 arrests
rfi.description: French authorities have arrested over 890 people after outbreaks of violence followed Paris Saint-Germain’s Champions League victory on Saturday, as the government defended its policing operation amid sharp criticism from the right.

rfi.title: France boards fourth Russian oil tanker as crackdown on ‘shadow fleet’ continues
rfi.description: The French Navy has boarded another oil tanker from Russia as Paris steps up its campaign against Moscow’s so-called "shadow fleet" of vessels suspected of evading international sanctions.

rfi.title: France weighs tougher safeguards against child abuse in schools
rfi.description: French lawmakers will on Monday debate tougher protections against sexual abuse in schools and after-school programmes, as a series of scandals increases pressure on the government to strengthen safeguards.

rfi.title: First contact: Curaçao’s rise to the global stage
rfi.description: Curaçao will make its World Cup debut at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada. In the first instalment of a four-part series, RFI looks at the journey of the smallest nation to qualify for the competition in its 96-year history.

rfi.title: France requests emergency UN meeting amid Israeli advance in Lebanon
rfi.description: France has requested an emergency meeting of the United Nations Security Council after Israeli forces seized the medieval Beaufort castle in Lebanon, the French foreign minister said Sunday.

rfi.title: Ethiopia election overshadowed by war, instability and muted opposition
rfi.description: Ethiopia goes to the polls on Monday in an election which is expected to return Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s Prosperity Party to power, but has been marked by instability, restricted voting and questions over whether the vote can challenge the status quo.

euronews.title: Iran World Cup squad to head for Mexico via Spain
euronews.description: Iran’s national football team will travel to Spain before heading to its World Cup base in Mexico, despite players still awaiting Mexican and US visas ahead of the 2026 tournament. The 2026 World Cup is being hosted jointly by the United States, Mexico and Canada.

euronews.title: 'La Caverne du Pont-Neuf' damaged by wind, opening postponed
euronews.description: The temporary artwork failed to withstand Tuesday afternoon's high winds and heavy downpours, and will no longer open to the public on 6 June as planned.

euronews.title: Russia may launch another large scale attack against Ukraine tonight, Zelenskyy warns
euronews.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy issued a stark warning on Tuesday evening saying that according to Ukraine’s intelligence Russia may launch another large-scale aerial attack tonight. It comes as Moscow is exploiting a critical shortage of air defence interceptor missiles.

euronews.title: Health ministry approves new framework statute despite health workers' strike call in Spain
euronews.description: The government says the main trade unions back the reform, despite months of protests by professionals across the political spectrum. The draft law still needs Congress approval.

euronews.title: 'Murcia deploys Military Emergencies Unit to Espuña fire and calls for better coordination'
euronews.description: The fire has led Murcia’s government to put the Military Emergency Unit on alert and raise the Infomur plan to level 2, as regional and central authorities swap messages over the need for coordination.

euronews.title: European Commission is set to criticise Italy for weak industrial strategy
euronews.description: The Commission will criticise Italy’s lack of robust industrial plans and calls for measures to incentivise investment in capital markets as well as reform of tax system, in country-specific recommendations to be published tomorrow.

euronews.title: ‘You’re f****** crazy’: Trump clashes with Netanyahu as Lebanon tensions rise
euronews.description: Trump rebukes Benjamin Netanyahu over Lebanon escalation, warning strikes risk isolating Israel and derailing Iran talks, according to reports

euronews.title: Explained: How drone incursions in Europe went from rarity to reality
euronews.description: A drone strike in Romania has reignited fears that Russia’s war in Ukraine is spilling into Europe. As incursions multiply across NATO and EU member states, leaders are racing to strengthen defences against a growing threat that blends military pressure, disruption and psychological warfare.

euronews.title: Why is the EU establishing return hubs for migrants — and why are they so controversial?
euronews.description: The new migration law approved on Monday allows EU countries to establish return centres outside the bloc. But critics warn it could lead to human rights violations, while governments are seeking partner countries to host the facilities.

euronews.title: IRGC says Iran has more 'trump cards' up its sleeve as talks hang by a thread
euronews.description: A senior IRGC general said Iran had not revealed all its military capabilities and was ready for direct confrontation with the US and NATO, as hardliners linked to acting IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi were identified as the force behind Monday's suspension of indirect negotiations with Washington.

euronews.title: Spanish waters hit 'historic records' in May after extreme heatwave
euronews.description: State Ports' monitoring networks recorded all-time May temperature highs at 18 of their 29 buoys, from Galicia and the Cantabrian coast to the Mediterranean, peaking at 26.58°C off Mahon.

euronews.description: The rapid reshape of global energy supply routes and markets is a key focus at the Baku Energy Week 2026.

euronews.description: The seizure is the latest evidence of France's efforts to crack down on vessels suspected of helping Russia evade sanctions imposed following Moscow's invasion of Ukraine.

euronews.title: Czech police charge four in OnlyFans human trafficking case
euronews.description: Young women who had just turned 18 were lured into creating erotic photos and videos before signing management contracts with the perpetrators, who promised to grow their careers.

euronews.title: A blood test could flag Alzheimer’s risk early. But how reliable is it?
euronews.description: Scientists have developed a blood test that could spot signals of Alzheimer's disease at a much younger age.

euronews.title: €25 million invested, €150 million earned: the 'miraculous' return on the Pope's visit
euronews.description: In what it hails as a loaves-and-fishes miracle, the Spanish Bishops' Conference says Pope Leon XIV’s trip to Spain will bring in five times its cost, though less than the 2011 visit’s 354 million euros.

euronews.title: EU Commission set to slam Italy's fuel duty cuts as energy prices spike
euronews.description: The EU Commission is set to criticise the Italian government's reduction in excise duties on fuels in a report to be published on Wednesday. Rome has been asking for more fiscal flexibility to address the energy crisis, which Brussels deems should be directed at vulnerable families and industries.

lemonde.description: « Face à un pouvoir répressif » (3/3). Six ans après la fin du grand mouvement prodémocratie qui a ébranlé le pays, le harcèlement judiciaire est toujours à l’œuvre contre ceux qui continuent à promouvoir la liberté d’expression.

lemonde.title: De Neuilly à la frontière suisse, ces 20 villes où se concentrent les Français aisés
lemonde.description: La commune des Hauts-de-Seine est la ville française qui compte la plus forte proportion de ménages à très hauts revenus, selon une étude de l’Observatoire des inégalités, publiée mardi 2 juin. Le classement est dominé par l’Ouest parisien et les abords de Genève.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Volodymyr Zelensky met en garde contre « une frappe massive qui pourrait avoir lieu cette nuit » au lendemain de bombardements massifs russes
lemonde.description: « Nous savons, grâce aux services de renseignement, qu’une frappe massive pourrait avoir lieu cette nuit. Je vous en prie, soyez attentifs aux sirènes d’alerte aérienne », a insisté le président ukrainien dans une allocution vidéo diffusée mardi soir.

lemonde.title: Les fruits et légumes bio associés à une baisse du risque de cancer du sein post-ménopause
lemonde.description: Selon des travaux français, pour chaque portion de 100 grammes de fruits et légumes conventionnels remplacés quotidiennement par leurs équivalents issus de l’agriculture biologique, le risque de développer un cancer du sein post-ménopausique est réduit de 10 %.

lemonde.title: Crise énergétique : l’Italie obtient un aménagement minimal du pacte de stabilité et de croissance
lemonde.description: Les Etats membres pourront, sous certaines conditions, utiliser jusqu’à 0,3 % de leur produit intérieur brut par an pour aider les entreprises et les ménages à faire face à la flambée des prix de l’énergie.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, Roland-Garros 2026 : Jakub Mensik remporte le deuxième set face à Joao Fonseca et se rapproche des demi-finales
lemonde.description: Plus tôt, l’Allemand Alexander Zverev a battu l’Espagnol Rafael Jodar et a rallié le dernier carré du tournoi. Ce mardi a commencé par les deux premiers quarts féminins, et les qualifications de la Russe Mirra Andreeva et de l’Ukrainienne Marta Kostyuk.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : le Hezbollah est le « seul obstacle » à la paix entre Israël et le Liban, selon le chef de la diplomatie américaine, Marco Rubio
lemonde.description: « Israël et le Liban pourraient conclure un accord de paix dès demain. Israël n’a aucune revendication territoriale au Liban », a affirmé mardi Marco Rubio, lors d’une audition devant la commission des affaires étrangères du Sénat américain. lemonde.title: Génocide des Tutsi : un mémorial inauguré à Paris par Emmanuel Macron et Paul Kagame
lemonde.description: Le président français a inauguré mardi sur les quais de la Seine un monument en hommage aux victimes du génocide de 1994. Son homologue rwandais a salué un travail de mémoire sans équivalent dans le monde.

lemonde.title: Une étude met en lumière la trop lente féminisation du journalisme sportif
lemonde.description: L’association Femmes journalistes de sport publie, mardi 2 juin, une étude chiffrée sur la quasi-absence d’évolution des rédactions vers davantage de parité au sein des rubriques sportives.

lemonde.title: Projet de loi contre l’antisémitisme : le gouvernement veut aussi dans ce cadre protéger les fonctionnaires
lemonde.description: Selon une information du « Monde », le gouvernement va intégrer dans le projet de loi de lutte contre l’antisémitisme, attendu avant l’été, une disposition permettant aux administrations de déposer plainte au nom de leurs agents victimes de violences ou de menaces.

lemonde.title: « Face au RN, le secteur du lobbying doit se doter d’une doctrine minimale de responsabilité démocratique »
lemonde.description: Le lobbyiste Jordan Allouche s’inquiète, dans une tribune au « Monde », du rôle croissant que jouent les milieux d’affaires et patronaux dans la montée en puissance de l’extrême droite. Il appelle les cabinets de conseil en affaires publiques à refuser de participer à la normalisation du Rassemblement national.

lemonde.description: La nouvelle promotion du label d’Etat « Palaces de France » a été révélée mardi 2 juin, avec six entrées et quatre sorties. Une manière de valoriser ce secteur vitrine du savoir-faire hexagonal, même si les propriétaires de ces établissements sont rarement français.

lemonde.title: Les Nuits de Fourvière, à Lyon, offrent une programmation effervescente pour les 80 ans du festival
lemonde.description: Jusqu’au 25 juillet, 60 spectacles, concerts, performances et bals masqués en plein air sont proposés, parmi lesquels « Revoir les étoiles », de la troupe de cirque australienne Circa.

lemonde.title: « Not Suitable for Work » sur Disney+, portrait drôle et tendre d’une génération Z new-yorkaise déboussolée
lemonde.description: Après « Mes premières fois », Mindy Kaling revient avec une nouvelle série qui met en scène cinq jeunes célibataires habitant le même immeuble de Manhattan.

france24fr.title: Remaniement ministériel au Sénégal : une nouvelle équipe de 30 ministres dont 4 femmes

Une équipe sans la participation du Pastef, le parti dirigé par son ancien Premier ministre, nouveau président de l'Assemblée nationale et compagnon de route de longue date, Ousmane Sonko. Un gouvernement de 30 ministres dont 4 femmes.

france24fr.title: Pollution au chlordécone aux Antilles : le Parlement reconnaît une responsabilité de l'État
france24fr.description: Le Parlement a adopté, mardi, une proposition de loi visant à reconnaître la "part de responsabilité" de l'État dans le scandale du chlordécone aux Antilles, malgré une ambition amoindrie en cours d'examen au Sénat.

france24fr.title: Une proposition de loi pour limiter l'exposition des Français au cadmium
france24fr.description: Les Français sont surexposés au cadmium, responsable notamment de l'augmentation des cancers du pancréas. Ce métal lourd est répandu dans les champs par le biais des engrais phosphatés. La concentration maximale autorisée en France est de 90mg de cadmium par kilo d'engrais. L'ANSES préconise un plafond à 20mg seulement. Une proposition de loi a été adoptée en commission à l'Assemblée Nationale. Elle vise à réduire drastiquement les concentrations autorisées.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : même sans Sonko, le président Diomaye Faye a des chances de gouverner sans blocages
france24fr.description: Le président sénégalais, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, a fait, lundi, un pas supplémentaire vers la rupture avec son ex-Premier ministre Ousmane Sonko en formant, sans son assentiment pour une particpation du Pastef, un nouveau gouvernement. Selon les analystes, l'exécutif pourrait toutefois fonctionner sans subir de blocage décisif de son ex-allié.

france24fr.title: Cancer du pancréas : le daraxonrasib, un espoir pour retarder la progression de la maladie
france24fr.description: Présenté au congrès international d'oncologie de Chicago, un nouveau traitement contre le cancer du pancréas, le daraxonrasib, a été accueilli comme "un progrès majeur". Pour cause, cet anticancéreux pourrait doubler l'espérance de vie de certains patients et ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives pour le traitement d'autres cancers. Explications.

france24fr.title: Guerre hybride : l'atout de Poutine ?
france24fr.description: En Ukraine, la guerre se poursuit. La Russie multiplie ses offensives et a mené, la nuit dernière, une attaque de drones contre le territoire ukrainien. Parallèlement, le pétrolier russe Tagor, en provenance de Mourmansk et arraisonné par la Marine nationale ce week-end, est arrivé ce matin en baie de Douarnenez. Dans le même temps, à l’est de l’Europe, un drone russe chargé d’explosifs a pénétré l’espace aérien roumain avant de s’écraser sur un immeuble, faisant deux blessés.

france24fr.title: Au nom de la cybersécurité, Donald Trump finit par réguler l'IA
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a signé, mardi, un décret très attendu instituant un encadrement de l'IA aux États-Unis, au nom de la cybersécurité. Le texte entend notamment protéger les systèmes informatiques du pays face à des modèles d'IA désormais capables de repérer et d'exploiter des failles à une vitesse inédite.

france24fr.title: Bill Pulte, un fidèle de Trump inexpérimenté, à la tête du renseignement national
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a nommé mardi l'un de ses fidèles, Bill Pulte, au poste stratégique de directeur du renseignement national. Cette décision fait craindre aux démocrates une intensification des poursuites contre les adversaires politiques du président.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle : ces images ne prouvent pas que le premier meeting de Gabriel Attal a été un “bide”
france24fr.description: Des internautes pro-russes affirment que le premier meeting pour la présidentielle 2027 de l’ancien Premier ministre français Gabriel Attal aurait été un échec : ils partagent comme preuves de prétendues photographies montrant un public clairsemé. Mais ces images ont été générées par intelligence artificielle.

france24fr.title: Union européenne : quatre questions sur les "hubs de retour" de migrants
france24fr.description: L’Union européenne devrait bientôt permettre à ses États membres de créer des "hubs de retour" dans des pays tiers, qui auront pour but d’accueillir les étrangers en situation irrégulière expulsés du territoire européen. Le texte est considéré comme une avancée en matière de politique migratoire par la droite et l’extrême droite, et comme un recul pour les droits humains par la gauche. Explications.

france24fr.title: ⚽Mondial 2026 : Macron rend visite aux Bleus à Clairefontaine
france24fr.description: 🇫🇷 À quelques jours du début de la Coupe du monde, le président Emmanuel #Macron s'est rendu à #Clairefontaine pour soutenir l'équipe de #France, qui s'envolera bientôt pour New York afin d'y disputer son premier match contre le Sénégal le 16 juin.⚽

france24fr.title: Quand la Chine rêve d’identifier les futurs opposants politiques grâce à l’IA
france24fr.description: L’entreprise chinoise Geedge Network, déjà accusée d’avoir vendu le système de censure numérique chinois à d’autres pays, planche également sur la possibilité de laisser l’IA déceler qui pourrait à l'avenir devenir un opposant politique. Un rêve pour tout régime autoritaire et un cauchemar pour les défenseurs des droits humains ?

france24fr.title: L'ONU alerte sur un probable épisode du phénomène El Niño "modéré voir fort" cet été
france24fr.description: Le développement d'un épisode El Niño est probable à 80% entre juin et août, augmentant le risque d'événements météorologiques extrêmes dans les prochains mois, a alerté mardi l'Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM).

france24fr.title: Malgré les promesses de désescalade, Israël mène des attaques meurtrières au Sud-Liban
france24fr.description: Israël a poursuivi ses frappes sur le Sud-Liban mardi, faisant plusieurs morts dont des enfants, au lendemain de la demande du président américain, Donald Trump, au Premier ministre israélien, Benjamin Netanyahu, de ne pas attaquer Beyrouth afin d'éviter une nouvelle escalade.

france24fr.title: Avec le Salon Computex, Taiwan est le berceau de la révolution IA
france24fr.description: Le président taiwanais a inauguré le salon “Computex” basé sur les nouvelles technologies.  L'événement se décrit comme la plus grande exposition sur l'IA jamais réalisée et se déroule sur l'île devenue au fil des années une super star de l'intelligence artificielle. Un atout sur lequel se base le gouvernement taiwanais pour assurer sa sauvegarde politique à l'échelle internationale.

france24fr.title: Rwanda-France : un mémorial pour les victimes du génocide inaugurée à Paris
france24fr.description: Ce mardi 2 juin, le chef de l'État rwandais, Paul Kagame, se rend dans la capitale française pour inaugurer en compagnie d'Emmanuel Macron une double stèle en mémoire des victimes du génocide des Tutsis au Rwanda. Un nouveau geste mémoriel de Paris pour sceller la réconciliation entre les deux pays.

france24fr.title: Les pourparlers reprennent : quatrième cycle de négociations entre Israël et le Liban
france24fr.description: Les ambassadeurs d'Israël et du Liban ont été reçus mardi au département d'Etat pour une nouvelle session de pourparlers directs, alors qu'Israël et le Hezbollah ont échangé des tirs après que Donald Trump a affirmé avoir reçu l'engagement d'un apaisement de la part des deux camps. spiegel.title: Donald Trump: US-Regierung soll exklusiven Vorabzugang zu neuen KI-Modellen bekommen
spiegel.description: Der anfängliche Widerstand aus der Techbranche ist offenbar beigelegt: Präsident Donald Trump will US-Behörden bedeutende KI-Zugänge verschaffen. Das hat auch mit einem neuen Hackingwerkzeug zu tun.

spiegel.title: Ehegattensplitting: Wirtschaftsexperten fordern von der Bundesregierung Obergrenze
spiegel.description: In einem offenen Brief an Kanzler Merz und Vizekanzler Klingbeil schlagen namhafte Wirtschaftsforschende eine Reform des Ehegattensplittings vor: Weil sich Mehrarbeit oft kaum lohnt, soll der Steuervorteil gedeckelt werden.

spiegel.title: Libanon: Israel gelingt symbolischer Sieg an Kreuzfahrerburg Beaufort
spiegel.description: Zum zweiten Mal nach 44 Jahren hat Israels Armee die Kreuzfahrerburg Beaufort im Südlibanon eingenommen, die Hisbollah reagiert mit tödlichen Drohnenattacken. Der Ort droht erneut zum Sinnbild eines endlosen Krieges zu werden.

spiegel.title: Polen plant Handyverbot an Grundschulen
spiegel.description: Zum kommenden Schuljahr will Polen Handys aus Grundschulen verbannen. Die Regierung in Warschau hat dafür einen Gesetzentwurf auf den Weg gebracht – auch auf Wunsch vieler Lehrkräfte.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: Polizisten legten Sterbendem Handschellen an – Video löst Rassismusdebatte aus
spiegel.description: Ein 23-Jähriger aus der Sikh-Gemeinschaft sticht auf einen 18-Jährigen ein. Als die Polizei eintrifft, hält sie aber zunächst den verletzten Teenager für den Täter. Bodycamaufnahmen lösen in Großbritannien einen Aufschrei aus.

spiegel.title: Stanley Cup und Pokémon: Die Sammelleidenschaft der Vegas Golden Knights
spiegel.description: Das Eishockeyteam Vegas Golden Knights steht im Finale des Stanley Cups. Sollte ihnen der Gewinn der Meisterschaft gelingen, hat das eventuell auch ein bisschen mit Pikachu, Schiggy und Glurak zu tun.

spiegel.title: Commerzbank: UniCredit steigert Anteil auf über ein Drittel
spiegel.description: Die feindliche Übernahme der Commerzbank durch die UniCredit schreitet voran. Die Italiener bauen ihren Anteil auf mehr als 34 Prozent aus und überschreiten damit die wichtige 30-Prozent-Schwelle.

spiegel.title: Radikale Islamisten: »Dschihadisten«, die zu allem entschlossen sind - SPIEGEL TV
spiegel.description: Sie haben Hass auf die freie westliche Welt. Das Bundeskriminalamt nennt sie »Gefährder«. Mahmoud Mhemed gehörte für die Beamten nicht dazu. Sein Anschlag auf einen Nachtclub in Bielefeld kam fast aus dem Nichts.

spiegel.title: Serena Williams spielt wieder Tennis: Das Wiederkommen ist so viel leichter als das Aufhören
spiegel.description: Nach vierjähriger Pause kehrt Serena Williams ins Profitennis zurück, mit nunmehr 44 Jahren – an der Seite einer 19-jährigen Doppelpartnerin. Warum macht sie das?

spiegel.title: Brasilien: Warum der Fußball schon an den Namen erkennbar ist
spiegel.description: Zico, Garrincha, Tostão: Früher waren Brasiliens Spitznamen ein Versprechen. Heute klingt die Seleção austauschbar. Schuld daran: Vermarktung, Agentenlogik, der Zeitgeist.

spiegel.title: Alexander Zverev: Wie der Tennisstar zur Antithese der French Open wird
spiegel.description: Während Roland Garros in Favoritenstürzen und Fünfsatzmatches versinkt, lässt sich Alexander Zverev nicht aus der Ruhe bringen. Auch nicht vom 19-jährigen Rafael Jódar und einer besonderen Geräuschkulisse.

spiegel.title: Rheinmetall: Rumänien bestellt Waffen und Munition im Wert von 5,7 Milliarden Euro
spiegel.description: Rheinmetall hat nach eigenen Angaben den größten internationalen Auftrag der jüngeren Unternehmensgeschichte angenommen. Darunter: Panzer, Munition und Schiffe.

spiegel.title: Rostock – Fall Fabian: Angeklagte wendet Blick von grausamen Tatortfotos ab
spiegel.description: Ein Feldweg, hohes Gebüsch, dahinter der leblose Körper: Im Prozess um den gewaltsamen Tod des achtjährigen Fabian geht es um grausame Fotos vom Tatort. Die Verteidigung gibt sich gelassen.

spiegel.title: Yad Vashem in Deutschland: Streit um Einflussnahme und deutsche Erinnerungslücken – ein Debattenbeitrag von Deborah Hartmann
spiegel.description: Deutschland bekommt zwei Außenstellen von Yad Vashem. Nach der Entscheidung warnen Kritiker vor israelischer Einflussnahme. Dabei zeigt ausgerechnet der Protest, wie groß die Leerstellen im deutschen Holocaustgedenken sind.

spiegel.title: Uno-Generalversammlung: Khalilur Rahman übernimmt von Annalena Baerbock »einen der besten Jobs der Welt«
spiegel.description: Ab September wird Khalilur Rahman neuer Präsident der Uno-Vollversammlung und folgt auf Annalena Baerbock. Der früheren Außenministerin attestieren Experten in ihrer Amtszeit eine »zupackende Führungspersönlichkeit«.

spiegel.title: FDP: Wolfgang Kubicki und Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann - Ausgleich nach Machtkampf
spiegel.description: Nach dem Duell um den Vorsitz flogen verbale Spitzen, nun senden der neue FDP-Chef Kubicki und die unterlegene Strack-Zimmermann versöhnliche Töne. Kann der Frieden halten?

spiegel.title: Donald Trump soll Benjamin Netanyahu wüst beschimpft haben
spiegel.description: Weil Israel im Libanon weiter angreifen will, soll US-Präsident Trump seinen Verbündeten scharf angegangen sein: »You’re fucking crazy« soll er zu Netanyahu gesagt haben. Währenddessen gehen die Kampfhandlungen offenbar weiter.

nyt.title: New Proposal Would Allow Administration to Block Grants if They Don’t Support Trump’s Agenda
nyt.description: A new proposal would allow the administration to block grants if they do not satisfy President Trump’s agenda or support what it calls “anti-American” values.

nyt.title: Trump Names Bill Pulte as Acting Director of National Intelligence
nyt.description: Bill Pulte, a Trump loyalist who leads the federal housing finance agency, will oversee the U.S. intelligence agencies. He has no known background in intelligence.

nyt.title: Trump Signs Executive Order Seeking Oversight of A.I. Models
nyt.description: The order, which signaled a shift from the hands-off approach the White House had previously taken toward A.I., followed debates over how to gain control of A.I. models without disrupting innovation.

nyt.title: Polls of California Governor’s Race Show a Clear Top 3
nyt.description: Xavier Becerra, Steve Hilton and Tom Steyer have consistently led the field in California’s nonpartisan primary, where the top two finishers advance.

nyt.title: What to Watch in Tuesday’s Primary Elections in Iowa, Montana and Beyond
nyt.description: Democrats have a competitive Senate primary race in Iowa, where the party is hoping to make gains, while a smokejumper is running in a contested House primary in Montana.

nyt.title: ‘Did I Have a Choice?’ In New Jersey, Kean Voters Explain Themselves.
nyt.description: Some Republicans outside polling sites acknowledged how strange it felt to cast a ballot for Representative Thomas Kean Jr., who has not been seen in public for months.

nyt.title: Only the Right Tests Can Stop This Ebola Outbreak. Congo Has Hardly Any.
nyt.description: A chronic lack of investment in development of better tests has left clinicians blind and allows deadly viruses to spread unchecked.

nyt.title: U.S. Ebola Unit Plans in Kenya, Subject of Protests, Suffers New Setback From Court Ruling
nyt.description: The court further delayed the Trump administration’s proposed quarantine unit for Americans exposed to the virus. The plan has sparked angry protests in Kenya.

nyt.title: How Three Chess Friends Battled Demons and Saved Two Lives
nyt.description: A homeless chess hustler, a scholar and an aging recluse found hope in a trashed apartment by Central Park.

nyt.title: Bombs Raining Down on Ukraine Can’t Hide Signs of Russia’s Faltering War
nyt.description: The war has not been going the Kremlin’s way, with battleground losses and growing casualties. With fiercer strikes, Moscow hopes to gain a better position for negotiations.

nyt.title: Russia Launches Deadly Strikes on Kyiv After Threatening Ukraine for a Week
nyt.description: Moscow’s repeated warnings of a major strike, combined with the delay before it happened, seemed intended to inflict a psychological toll on the Ukrainian capital.

nyt.title: The Toll of a ‘Missing Scientists’ Conspiracy Theory on the Families Left Behind
nyt.description: The claim that their loved ones’ deaths and disappearances are linked is almost certainly false — but the loss remains real.

nyt.title: Obama Center’s Two Sides: A Lovely Park and a Forbidding Tower
nyt.description: In Chicago, the $850 million Obama Presidential Center aims to remake a neighborhood with a 19.3-acre community hub and a brooding 225-foot museum.

nyt.title: What Ireland and Germany Can Teach Us About Birthright Citizenship
nyt.description: President Trump has argued that the United States is “stupid” for granting citizenship at birth. Most countries don’t do so, but that can create problems.

nyt.title: Carney Says Canada Faces a ‘Crisis of Antisemitism’
nyt.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s comments followed calls for action from Jewish organizations and after a government report found that antisemitism had surged in Canada in recent years.

nyt.title: ‘La La Land’ Orchestral Performance Saved by Keyboardist in the Audience
nyt.description: After a musician fell ill during a live performance of the score from “La La Land,” the composer Justin Hurwitz asked for a sight reader. A 21-year-old student stepped up.

nyt.title: Netanyahu’s Critics Accuse Him of Running Israel as a U.S. ‘Vassal State’
nyt.description: Critics pounced on the Israeli prime minister after President Trump claimed on social media he had persuaded him to call off “a major raid” on Hezbollah in Beirut.

nyt.title: In Her Memoir, Jill Biden Is a Watchful Spouse Who Didn’t Always Speak Up About Joe Biden
nyt.description: The former first lady’s new book reflects an insular White House where loyalty was prized and President Joseph R. Biden Jr.’s feelings were prioritized over health concerns.

npr.title: Scenes from the aftermath of Russia's latest massive attack on Kyiv
npr.description: Russian missile and drone attacks killed  civilians across Ukraine overnight, in one of Moscow's largest assaults in recent months.

npr.title: EU strikes migration deal for more deportations and detention centers abroad
npr.description: The European Union has moved forward with an overhaul of its migration policy, aiming to ramp up deportations and build detention centers abroad. Critics compared the regulation to the immigration strategy of the Trump administration.

npr.title: Global conflicts push Sri Lanka's economy to the brink
npr.description: Sri Lanka was careening from crisis to crisis, then came the Mideast war. People say they've got no buffer left.

npr.title: Ultra-Orthodox protesters block roads and trains across Israel over military draft
npr.description: Tens of thousands of ultra-Orthodox demonstrated across Israel on Monday, blocking roads and trains and setting cars on fire to protest mandatory enlistment in Israel's military.

npr.title: What to know about U.S. military strikes on alleged drug boats
npr.description: The U.S. military strikes on alleged drug boats have killed over 200 people. The attacks began in September and aim to stem drug flow, but critics question their legality and effectiveness.

npr.title: Russian attack on Ukraine kills 22 people, officials say, as Moscow escalates fighting
npr.description: Russian forces launched a massive aerial attack on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, and officials say at least 22 civilians were killed and 138 were wounded. The assault began overnight and continued during the day.

npr.title: Iran halts talks with U.S. over Israeli actions in Lebanon, Gaza
npr.description: Trumps says Israel and Hezbollah will stop fighting after Iran stops talks with U.S. over Israeli operations in southern Lebanon, Gaza

npr.title: U.S. strikes Iranian military sites. And, Trump's $1.8 billion fund faces scrutiny
npr.description: American aircraft fired on a number of Iranian sites over the weekend, including Qeeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. And, Trump's anti-weaponization fund faces scrutiny in Congress and the courts.

npr.title: Confirmed Ebola cases in Congo near 300 as survivors describe their recoveries
npr.description: The outbreak remains focused in Congo's eastern Ituri province. Congo has reported over 1,000 suspected cases with the Bundibugyo virus, which has no approved treatment or vaccine.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

undark.title: Medicine’s Move Toward Race-Neutral Risk Assessments
undark.description: Earlier this year, new guidelines were released for doctors assessing a patient’s risk for heart disease. The guidelines take a race-neutral and patient-informed approach that’s rooted in up-to-date science, one doctor writes, and offer a glimpse of a future in which health equity is the standard in medicine.

undark.title: In Coal Country, Black Lung Surges as Federal Protections Stall
undark.description: While the Trump administration is directing hundreds of millions of dollars to coal projects, miners in Appalachia are suffering from a resurgence of black lung disease. But industry pushback is delaying federal rules that would reduce miners’ exposure to deadly silica dust.

phys-org.title: Environmental engineers reshape understanding of airborne pollution particles
phys-org.description: From sizzling bacon in the kitchen to wildfire smoke in the sky, cooking and pollution release microscopic particles that affect humans' health, the air they breathe, and even weather and climate. New research from Virginia Tech is poised to upend how scientists think about the structure of these tiny airborne droplets and what that means for predictions around air quality, pollution spread, and climate models.

phys-org.title: Municipal partnership systems and mental health among sexual minorities in Japan: A nationwide analysis
phys-org.description: Although same-sex marriage has not been legalized nationally in Japan, various municipal governments have independently introduced partnership certification systems for same-sex couples.

phys-org.title: Embryonic tissues can behave like fluids or solids to reshape cell fate signals
phys-org.description: Embryonic development is one of the most dynamic biological processes in nature. Cells and tissues organize and reorganize themselves following incredibly precise patterns, while remaining flexible and robust. Scientists are increasingly probing the role the physical properties of embryonic tissues—such as rigidity or stiffness—play in this process.

phys-org.title: France follows England in measuring hottest spring on record
phys-org.description: France experienced its hottest spring on record, the country's weather service said Tuesday, after an exceptional early heat wave that also broke seasonal highs in England and Wales.

phys-org.title: Amazon rainforest emits new stress-defense molecules during El Niño drought
phys-org.description: The Amazon rainforest responded to the most severe drought ever recorded in the basin with an unexpected defense mechanism. Researchers at the Max Planck Institute for Chemistry in Mainz, Germany, found that during and after the intense 2023–2024 El Niño cycle, the most intense drought ever recorded in the region, vegetation significantly changed its chemical emissions to cope with environmental stress. The study was published in Communications Earth & Environment.

phys-org.description: North Carolina's blueberry farmers may have a beetle problem. A new study from North Carolina State University has identified destructive beetles inhabiting North Carolina blueberry fields as Prionus imbricornus, a species of longhorn beetle. Known for their long antennae, the wood-boring beetles are an emerging pest in NC blueberries. Female adults typically lay their eggs in the soil near the roots of hardwood trees; their larvae, which can grow up to five inches long, then consume and de

phys-org.title: First human SMUG1 atomic snapshots reveal how cells repair DNA
phys-org.description: Researchers have captured the first atomic structures of human SMUG1, an enzyme that helps cells repair damaged DNA. The findings provide new insight into how cells recognize and remove harmful DNA bases, and may support future efforts to develop drugs that target this DNA repair pathway.

phys-org.title: Rare meteorite provides evidence of giant early planet
phys-org.description: Four-and-a-half billion years ago, a massive world—possibly as big as the moon or even Mars—orbited our sun before crashing into another celestial body and shattering into rubble. Now, in a paper published in the journal Earth and Planetary Science Letters, scientists report the first definitive evidence that this lost planetary embryo (protoplanet) existed. Its unique geological makeup challenges long-held assumptions about how planets evolve.

phys-org.title: The World Cup and human trafficking: What the research reveals about the real risks at major sporting events
phys-org.description: As U.S. cities prepare to host the FIFA World Cup, familiar warnings about human trafficking "spikes" at major sporting events have reemerged.

phys-org.title: Six roads to safety: A critical threshold for wildfire survival
phys-org.description: If your community was threatened by a wildfire, would you be able to quickly evacuate? A new study from UC Santa Barbara reveals that the number of roads out of a community may be one of the strongest predictors of wildfire fatalities, and that a surprisingly specific threshold separates high-risk communities from safer ones.

phys-org.title: Clean drinking water gaps linked to hunger and unsafe food worldwide
phys-org.description: A new global study has found that people without access to clean drinking water are significantly more likely to experience food insecurity and food safety threats, underscoring the urgent need for coordinated global action to address these issues together.

phys-org.title: Life in the ancient Arctic: Tiny teeth of newly discovered species suggest it was a cradle of mammalian evolution
phys-org.description: A fossil mammal tooth smaller than a grain of rice does not announce itself loudly. It must be hard won from sediment and stone. Then, under a microscope, it reveals itself—no longer just a speck of blackness but a surface of cusps, ridges, and worn edges.

phys-org.title: Lab evolution recreates COVID's path to omicron in months, reveals key conditions
phys-org.description: A key step in the origin of many pandemics occurs when an animal-borne virus infects humans and then evolves to spread more efficiently from person to person. That is why scientists and physicians keep a close watch on viruses that could jump from animals to humans, such as emerging strains of avian flu and bat coronaviruses, as well as viruses that have already crossed into humans but, for now, spread poorly among people, such as hantavirus and Ebola.

phys-org.title: Single cell transforms into cannibalistic 'supergiant,' swallowing its clones whole
phys-org.description: Researchers at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (RPI) have discovered a microscopic organism that can transform into a cannibalistic "supergiant" that drastically changes size, shape, and behavior, and abandons filter-feeding to hunt and consume their genetically identical relatives.

phys-org.title: Global supply chains keep workers poor: Three case studies show how the cycle can be broken
phys-org.description: Globally, about 1 in 5 people in jobs live in poverty. A key reason lies in how global supply chains are organized. From agriculture to tourism, many jobs are embedded in systems that keep wages low, even as they generate value for international markets.

phys-org.title: Kamo'oalewa asteroid's lunar origin challenged ahead of Tianwen-2 arrival
phys-org.description: China's Tianwen-2 sample-return mission is well on its way to its target, an asteroid called Kamo'oalewa. The spacecraft left Earth in May 2025 and should return in late 2027 with samples of a space rock that scientists had assumed originated from the moon. However, a new study published in Nature Communications suggests that we may be mistaken about the asteroid's origin.

phys-org.title: 'Genetic brakes' reveal how embryos shape their limbs
phys-org.description: Canadian scientists have made a significant advance in understanding the mechanisms that enable embryos to properly form their limbs, thanks to new research led by Université de Montréal medical professor Marie Kmita at the Montreal Clinical Research Institute (IRCM). phys-org.title: Fluorescent nanosensor detects key gut biomarker in minutes for faster testing
phys-org.description: A research collaboration has developed a novel fluorescent nanosensor capable of rapidly detecting indole-3-propionic acid (IPA), an emerging biomarker linked to gut health and disease. The breakthrough is described in the team's paper, "Fluorescent Nanosensor for Indole-3-Propionic Acid Detection in Gut Health Monitoring," published in the journal Advanced Healthcare Materials.

proj-syn.title: British Steel Needs a Transformation, Not a Bailout
proj-syn.description: The recent revival of industrial policy offers an opportunity to break the old pattern whereby economic risks are socialized while rewards remain privatized. In addition to attaching meaningful conditionalities to public support, governments must invest in the state capacity required to govern strategic sectors well.

proj-syn.title: How to Encourage Deceased Organ Donation
proj-syn.description: Developing countries facing organ shortages often search for complex solutions, such as sweeping legal reforms. But Tunisia’s experience suggests a much simpler first step: awareness-raising sessions where doctors explain how the transplant system works, and people share their fears and concerns.

proj-syn.title: Building Alliances of America’s Allies
proj-syn.description: In a world in which the US cannot be counted on as it once was, the objective is not stability at any price, but rather stability on terms consistent with national and Western interests. This is achievable, but only if the friends of the US recognize the new reality and act individually and collectively to meet the challenge.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Limits of African Data Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: African countries are recognizing that no matter how well-designed their data-protection regulations are, their sovereignty over US-based Big Tech firms ends at the boundary between subsidiary and parent. Overcoming this barrier will require a level of coordination that the continent has yet to achieve.

proj-syn.title: The AI Economy’s Permanent Underclass
proj-syn.description: AI is transforming the global economy while widening the gap between technological winners and losers. Governments that fail to secure a place in the AI supply chain may find themselves confronting mass job displacement without the tax revenues or state capacity needed to contain the social and political fallout.

proj-syn.title: The Rape of Venezuela
proj-syn.description: Venezuela’s oil production is rising, yet its currency is depreciating, inflation is accelerating, and foreign exchange remains scarce. The disconnect reflects a political economy built on private dealmaking and a mutually beneficial alliance between ruling elites and US President Donald Trump’s acolytes.

proj-syn.title: The One Man Who Could Give Trump Middle East Peace
proj-syn.description: With a large majority of UN member states recognizing Palestine on the 1967 lines, there is a clear international blueprint for creating an independent Palestinian state alongside Israel. What has been missing is credible Palestinian leadership of the kind that the imprisoned politician Marwan Barghouti could provide.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Nuclear Options
proj-syn.description: The risks raised by nuclear weapons remain as potent as ever, but the institutional framework that mitigated them has been severely eroded. The task now is to prevent deterrence from giving way to proliferation—which, for Europe, means building conventional capabilities, keeping the US engaged, and upholding restraint.

proj-syn.title: The Intelligence That AI Is Missing
proj-syn.description: For AI to simplify humans’ complex social and professional lives, it cannot just give tidy answers based on whatever the internet has to say about our values. It will need the capacity to account for our relational commitments, which are typically grounded in personal identity, experience, and culture.

proj-syn.title: Why Isn’t Europe Poorer Than the US?
proj-syn.description: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman has a point when he says that European living standards have largely kept pace with those in the US, despite flagging growth and innovation. But this will not remain true indefinitely: restoring Europe's ability to compete at the technological frontier remains essential to its future well-being.

proj-syn.title: The Real Choice Confronting Developing Countries
proj-syn.description: Lost in the debate about whether developing countries should pursue manufacturing- or services-led growth is the potential for new AI tools to make even informal workers far more productive. If governments can broaden access to such technologies, they no longer need to choose between strategies.

proj-syn.title: India’s Great Political Realignment
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party’s focus on religious identity, together with its “purification” of voter rolls, has created a more binary—and potentially volatile—political landscape, where elections increasingly reflect ethno-religious identity. This month’s elections in five states largely confirmed this trend.

proj-syn.title: Central Banking in an Age of Global Supply Shocks
proj-syn.description: The core assumptions underlying the decades-old inflation-targeting orthodoxy have proven to be unfit for a geopolitically fragmented world characterized by frequent supply-side disruptions.
